LESSON: GUIDED WRITING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: WRITING Theme 7: My body (Body functions) Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Ou
Topic 3.8: Guided writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 1

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided writing, part of WRITING Theme 7: My body (Body functions) Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Ou in Grade 5 GERMAN.

Key inquiry question: How important is labelling of pictures?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. spell words with correct orthography

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. formulate short simple sentences for comprehension

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop writing skills in German for enjoyment.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. spell words with correct orthography

   Guided writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. formulate short simple sentences for comprehension

   Guided writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. develop writing skills in German for enjoyment.

   Guided writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. label pictures of weather features and weather patterns and read out aloud to peers,

2. match phrases to appropriate picture of weather pattern,

3. organise jumbled up sentences in the right order/logically,

4. colour sketches of weather features and patterns.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. label pictures of weather features and weather patterns and read out aloud to peers,
2. match phrases to appropriate picture of weather pattern,
3. organise jumbled up sentences in the right order/logically,
4. colour sketches of weather features and patterns.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: Learner develops skills of logical writing when learner organises jumbled up sentences

to a logical comprehension text.

Values:
Love: Learner appreciates different weather patterns as the learner matches phrases to pictures of weather patterns.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Environmental Education: Learner demonstrates awareness of how weather patterns affect their lifestyles by matching

phrases to pictures on weather patterns.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner links the concept of weather and weather patterns to the same concept in Social Studies.
